harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (primary, writable), node2, and node3 (standbys, read-only) on AlmaLinux 9.6. Installed postgresql-server 16.14 via the AppStream module on all nodes, initdb'd node1, created a scram-sha-256 replicator role, enabled wal_level=replica/max_wal_senders/hot_standby, opened firewalld port 5432 for the cluster subnet, and cloned node2/node3 from node1 via pg_basebackup -R with dedicated replication slots (node2_slot, node3_slot). Verified a row inserted on the primary replicated to both standbys and that standbys reject writes as read-only. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured boot-ID baselines and healthy replication state on all three nodes, restarted node2, node3, then node1 one at a time (preserving quorum), proved each node's boot_id changed post-restart, and confirmed full recovery — postgresql active, correct recovery role, replication slots/walreceivers reconnected, and existing data intact — after each restart, finishing with a fresh post-restart write on the primary that replicated to both standbys.
actions_performed: Inspected OS/existing state on node1, node2, node3
Installed postgresql-server/contrib 16.14 via dnf module postgresql:16 on all three nodes
Ran postgresql-setup --initdb and enabled/started postgresql on node1
Generated a random replication password on node1 and created the 'replicator' ROLE WITH REPLICATION LOGIN

Configured postgresql.conf on node1 (listen_addresses, wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders=10, max_replication_slots=10, hot_standby=on) and appended pg_hba.conf rules for replication and app access from the cluster subnet, then restarted postgresql
Opened firewalld TCP/5432 on node1 for 10.100.181.0/24 after diagnosing 'No route to host' errors
Ran pg_basebackup -R -X stream -C with dedicated slots on node2 and node3 to clone node1 as standbys, then enabled/started postgresql on both
Verified pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both standbys streaming and pg_is_in_recovery()=true on node2/node3
Created repl_test table, inserted a row on node1, confirmed it appeared on node2 and node3, and confirmed INSERT is rejected on both standbys as read-only
Captured pre-restart boot_id, service-active state, and repl_test row count on all three nodes
Rebooted node2, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, confirmed postgresql active/in-recovery and data intact, confirmed node1 shows it streaming again
Rebooted node3, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, confirmed postgresql active/in-recovery and data intact, confirmed node1 shows it streaming again

Rebooted node1 (primary) last, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, confirmed postgresql active/not-in-recovery, inserted a new verification row, confirmed both standbys show it and are streaming

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 configured as read-only standbys via streaming replication
evidence.summary: pg_basebackup cloned both nodes with standby.signal + primary_conninfo, postgresql active, pg_is_in_recovery()=true on both, pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both streaming

evidence.requirement: Changes committed on primary visible on both standbys
evidence.summary: Row inserted on node1 appears on node2 and node3; standbys reject INSERT with read-only transaction error
